sample_unit: generative language models evaluated on five MCQA benchmarks

links.outcome: Model robustness to prompt perturbations and semantic paraphrases on clinical MCQA benchmarks
links.effect: Large models were more resilient than small models, but the assumptions of knowledge application and consistent answers under semantic consistency were globally invalidated, and small models were prone to memorization.
links.quote: While large models are more resilient to our perturbations compared to small models, we globally invalidate these assumptions, with implications for reasoning models.

links.outcome: Validity of clinical licensing-exam MCQA benchmarks for GLM clinical competence, including null-answer recognition
links.effect: All models showed significant failure in null-answer scenarios, and the benchmark assumptions (knowledge applied not memorized, consistent answers, recognizing no-answer situations) were invalidated.
links.quote: All models exhibit significant failure in null-answer scenarios.

screen.reason: Evaluates generative language model performance across five medical MCQA benchmarks using prompt perturbations to test robustness and reasoning assumptions, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
